requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on node1 port 8443 with a certificate
requirements.summary: nginx installed and configured with an 'ssl' server block on 8443 using /etc/nginx/ssl/cert.pem and key.pem. curl -sk https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returned HTTP 200 both at initial setup and at the pre-restart baseline, and the after-executor listening-sockets snapshot independently confirms nginx bound to 0.0.0.0:8443 and :::8443.

requirements.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
requirements.summary: A busybox-crond entry runs renew-cert.sh every minute; the script only reissues the cert when remaining validity drops below a 180s threshold (cert validity is 300s). cert-renew.log shows a renewal at 11:54:36 (expiry 11:59:36) and a further renewal at 11:59:00 (serial 1790683140, new expiry 12:04:00). The continuous probe (cmd-bc7cd978914e47bb) independently shows the live cert serial was already 1790683020 from 11:57:51 onward and changed to 1790683140 exactly at 11:59:01 without any manual intervention in that window, corroborating at least one fully unattended cron-triggered renewal cycle before expiry. The executor's claim of a third renewal at exactly 11:57:00 is plausible from the serial-value math (1790683020 corresponds to 11:57:00 UTC) but the explicit log line for that middle renewal was not visible in the truncated log excerpt shown.

requirements.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
requirements.summary: renew-cert.sh runs `nginx -t` then `nginx -s reload` (graceful reload, no drop of the listening socket) after each renewal. A continuous 2-second curl probe across the 11:59:00 renewal boundary shows unbroken HTTP 200 responses immediately before and after the cert serial changed (11:58:59 serial=...020 HTTP 200; 11:59:01 serial=...140 HTTP 200), directly demonstrating zero-downtime cert pickup during a real automatic rotation.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, restart, new boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 2057e0f8..., nginx/crond 'started', valid cert, HTTP 200, and persisted crontab. A native `reboot` was issued and acknowledged; subsequent polls hit connection reset/timeout confirming the node went down. Post-restart boot_id 9a2a2188... differs from baseline, matching the fixed after-prepare (2057e0f8...) vs after-executor (9a2a2188...) snapshot cross-check. Post-restart checks show nginx and crond auto-started, the crontab entry and cert/key persisted, HTTPS 8443 returned HTTP 200, and a manual re-run of renew-cert.sh confirmed the renewal mechanism remained intact.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct, corroborated evidence: HTTPS is served on node1:8443 with a valid cert, the cert renews automatically before expiry via a minute-interval cron job, and a continuous probe across a real automatic renewal shows zero-downtime pickup via graceful nginx reload. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also executed correctly and shows full recovery of services, cert, and cron config with a verified boot-identity change matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good but not perfect: a handful of small troubleshooting artifacts and test files were left in /tmp, and the default nginx port-80 listener was not disabled, none of which affect the core task outcome.
limitations: The explicit cert-renew.log line for the renewal that produced serial 1790683020 (~11:57:00) was not directly visible in the log excerpt due to display truncation; its occurrence is inferred from serial-value arithmetic and the continuous probe rather than a directly quoted log line.
Only one full renewal cycle (11:59:00→11:59:01) was directly observed end-to-end by the continuous zero-downtime probe; the first renewal window was covered by a shorter, separately-run probe.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutating commands map clearly to the task or restart protocol: package install, nginx/cron config, cert generation, and the reboot sequence. Several early troubleshooting commands (cmd-1289d118e5354a71, cmd-770ab253de0e4052, cmd-3c2e8e8fd1814307, cmd-3df2738ce348457a) were bounded date-parsing experiments needed to fix a broken renewal script, a legitimate corrective/prerequisite action, but they left low-risk residue: test certs /tmp/c.pem and /tmp/k.pem plus other operational artifacts (apk.log, cron.new, curlout.txt, o.txt, probe.log, probe.pid, reboot.log) are still present in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot and were never cleaned up. None are destructive, security-weakening, or in a service-affecting location. A background 6-minute curl probe loop (cmd-d93c6466c4dd4911) was launched and its PID file left in /tmp, though the process was implicitly terminated by the subsequent reboot. The default nginx config also left an unrequested plaintext server on port 80 listening (visible in the after-executor listening-sockets diff), a minor unintended exposure inherited from the default package config rather than a deliberate executor mutation.
